title: Interest Charges and APRs on Larkspur Credit Cards
content:
These are the cardmember terms that govern how interest is charged on the Larkspur Credit Cards and which APR applies.

## Terms

(a) **APRs.** Purchase and cash advance APRs are the Prime Rate plus the card's margins.

(b) **Charging interest.** Interest is charged at statement closing on the average daily balance of each balance type, at that balance type's APR.

(c) **Purchases and the grace period.** Purchases are interest-free when the previous statement balance was paid in full by its due date. Cash advances and balance transfers accrue interest from posting.

(d) **Introductory APRs.** Introductory APRs apply for the card's introductory cycles from opening. For balance transfers, they apply only when the transfer posts within the card's introductory balance transfer window (in calendar days) of opening.

(e) **Penalty APR.** The penalty APR may apply to new transactions only after notice. It may apply to existing balances only when a minimum payment is at least as many days late as the card's penalty APR trigger. It is removed from existing balances after the card's required number of consecutive on-time minimum payments.

(f) **Accounts that are charged interest.** Interest is charged only on an account in active, suspended or closed status with a balance.

The card's margins, introductory rates and cycles, balance transfer window, grace period and penalty APR terms are the figures in the card's product terms. The account record shows the purchase APR in force and whether the penalty APR applies.

## How the counts in term (e) are measured

- **Days late.** An account's days past due are the calendar days from the payment due date shown on the account to today. This applies when an amount past due above 0.00 is shown and that due date is earlier than today. Otherwise the account is 0 days past due.
- **Consecutive on-time minimum payments.** Count backwards from the latest payment due date on or before today. The count is the number of consecutive most recent due dates whose minimum payment was received by the due date and was not returned. A due date whose payment was late or returned ends the run.

## Status test for interest (term f)

This test is applied before interest is charged, against the account's own system record.

| Account status | Interest charged at statement closing? |
|---|---|
| Active, with a balance | Yes |
| Suspended, with a balance | Yes |
| Closed, with a balance | Yes |
| Applied, declined or charged off | No |
| Any status, with no balance | No |

## Hypothetical illustrations

All figures below are invented.

- **Balance transfer window.** Suppose a card's introductory balance transfer window were 45 days. A transfer posting 45 days after opening is within the window. One posting 46 days after opening is not, and does not get the introductory APR.
- **Penalty APR on existing balances.** Suppose the penalty APR trigger were 40 days late. A minimum payment 40 days late meets "at least" 40. One that is 39 days late does not, so the penalty APR may not yet apply to existing balances.
- **Removing the penalty APR.** Suppose the cure count were 4. Payments received on time for the four most recent due dates, with none returned, remove the penalty APR from existing balances. If the second most recent of those payments had been returned, the run would count only 1.
